Policy Name: Cigna ACDF (CMM-601: Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion)
Referred Sections: CMM-601.6: Repeat Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF) at the Same Level
Malposition or Failure of Implant/Instrumentation or Structural Bone Graft

Medical necessity indications.Guideline Category: Malposition or Failure of Implant/Instrumentation or Structural Bone Graft
Required findings: Post‑operative imaging (X‑ray, CT, or MRI) demonstrates malposition, migration, breakage, loosening, dislodgement, rod bending/breakage, loss of curve correction, or decompensation at the previously fused level
Imaging must be obtained after the initial ACDF and be reviewed by the ordering surgeon
No additional clinical symptom criteria are required beyond the imaging evidence
Medical necessity indications.Source: Repeat Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF) at the Same Level > Malposition or Failure of Implant/Instrumentation or Structural Bone Graft (S11.1.1)

Required findings: ≥6 months elapsed since the prior ACDF at the same level
Daily neck pain causing clinically significant functional impairment (e.g., inability to perform household chores, prolonged standing)
Physical examination findings that are concordant with the reported neck pain

Failure to achieve clinically meaningful improvement after BOTH of the following (unless contraindicated): prescription‑strength analgesics, steroids, gabapentinoids, and/or NSAIDs for 6 weeks AND a provider‑directed exercise program for 6 weeks
Post‑operative imaging performed ≥6 months after the prior fusion showing pseudoarthrosis at the requested level(s)
Post‑operative MRI/CT that correlates with symptoms
Absence of unmanaged significant mental or behavioral health disorders
Documentation of nicotine‑free status (never‑smoker or ≥6 weeks abstinent with objective cotinine test within normal range)
Medical necessity indications.Source: Repeat Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF) at the Same Level > Unremitting Neck Pain with Pseudoarthrosis (S11.1.2)

Required findings: ≥6 months elapsed since the prior ACDF at the same level
Daily pain causing functional impairment AND unremitting radicular pain to the shoulder girdle and/or upper extremity resulting in disability

Physical exam demonstrating any of: dermatomal sensory deficit, motor deficit (biceps/triceps weakness), reflex changes, shoulder abduction relief sign, or positive Spurling’s maneuver (or radicular pain without concordant objective findings)

Failure to achieve clinically meaningful improvement after at least TWO of the following (unless contraindicated): prescription‑strength analgesics/steroids/gabapentinoids/NSAIDs for 6 weeks, provider‑directed exercise program for 6 weeks, epidural steroid injection(s) or selective nerve root block(s) at the same level
Post‑operative imaging ≥6 months after prior fusion showing pseudoarthrosis at the requested level(s)

Post‑operative MRI/CT showing neural structure compression at the requested level(s) caused by herniated disc, synovial/arachnoid cyst, central/lateral/foraminal stenosis, or osteophytes, and that correlates with symptoms and exam
Absence of unmanaged significant mental or behavioral health disorders
Documentation of nicotine‑free status (never‑smoker or ≥6 weeks abstinent with objective cotinine test within normal range)
Medical necessity indications.Source: Repeat Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF) at the Same Level > Radiculopathy with Pseudoarthrosis (S11.1.3)

Required findings: ≥6 months elapsed since the prior ACDF at the same level

Symptoms of myelopathy such as upper/lower extremity weakness, numbness, pain, fine motor dysfunction (buttoning, handwriting), gait disturbance, new‑onset bowel/bladder dysfunction, or frequent falls

Physical exam demonstrating any of: grip‑and‑release test abnormality, ataxic gait, hyperreflexia, Hoffmann sign, Babinski sign, tandem walking ataxia, inverted brachial radial reflex, increased tone/spasticity, clonus, or myelopathic hand
Post‑operative imaging ≥6 months after prior fusion showing pseudoarthrosis at the requested level(s)
Post‑operative MRI/CT showing cervical spinal cord compression or cervical spinal stenosis that correlates with the patient’s symptoms and exam findings
Absence of unmanaged significant mental or behavioral health disorders
Documentation of nicotine‑free status (never‑smoker or ≥6 weeks abstinent with objective cotinine test within normal range)
Medical necessity indications.Source: Repeat Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF) at the Same Level > Myelopathy with Pseudoarthrosis (S11.1.4)

Non-Indications: Request for repeat ACDF performed <6 months after the prior fusion at the same level
Absence of imaging evidence of pseudoarthrosis or implant failure at the requested level(s)
Failure to document functional impairment or concordant physical exam findings for the reported symptoms
Insufficient trial of conservative therapy (e.g., less than 6 weeks of prescribed analgesics/NSAIDs or less than 6 weeks of a supervised exercise program when required)
Unmanaged significant mental health or behavioral health disorders (major depressive disorder, chronic pain syndrome, secondary gain, opioid or alcohol use disorder)
Current tobacco use or lack of objective cotinine verification confirming nicotine‑free status
Important criteria & exceptions: All indications require ≥6 months elapsed time since the prior ACDF at the same level
Nicotine‑free status must be documented either as never‑smoker or by objective cotinine testing confirming abstinence for ≥6 weeks
Patients must not have unmanaged significant mental or behavioral health disorders at the time of request

Conservative therapy trial requirements differ by indication: both analgesic and exercise programs for neck pain; at least two modalities (medication, exercise, epidural steroid/nerve block) for radiculopathy; no specific conservative trial listed for implant failure or myelopathy but mental health and nicotine criteria still apply
Imaging (X‑ray/CT/MRI) confirming pseudoarthrosis or implant failure must be performed no earlier than 6 months after the initial fusion
Documentation required: Operative report of the initial anterior cervical discectomy and fusion
Post‑operative plain radiographs, CT, and/or MRI performed ≥6 months after the initial fusion showing pseudoarthrosis or implant malposition/failure
Radiology report describing the specific findings (pseudoarthrosis, hardware migration, breakage, neural compression, etc.)
Comprehensive physical examination note documenting pain severity, functional limitation, and any neurologic deficits (sensory, motor, reflex, myelopathic signs)
Pain and functional assessment documentation (e.g., pain scale, activities of daily living impact)

Records of conservative management: prescription records for analgesics/steroids/gabapentinoids/NSAIDs with duration ≥6 weeks, physical therapy or chiropractic treatment notes confirming ≥6 weeks of supervised exercise, and/or epidural steroid injection or selective nerve root block reports (for radiculopathy)
Mental health evaluation confirming absence of unmanaged significant psychiatric or substance use disorders

Nicotine use verification: smoking history statement indicating never‑smoker status OR cotinine test result (serum, urine, or saliva) performed within the last 6 weeks and reported as within normal range
Any prior imaging reports that demonstrate the timeline (to confirm the >6‑month interval)
